news.headline: RBI unveils toughest rupee defence since 2013: dollar window for oil firms, 20% reserve on hedges
news.summary: RBI will supply oil marketing companies' dollar needs from reserves from 12-Oct, require a 20% FX risk reserve on hedges above $2m, cut the no-underlying derivative limit to $5m and bar rebooking. Rupee rose ~0.6% in thin NDF trade. A stronger INR lowers MCX gold in rupee terms.
news.source: Reuters via Business Recorder / Business Today

news.headline: Iran says US response on reopening Hormuz is 'insufficient'; strait to stay shut until conditions met
news.summary: SNSC head Mohsen Rezaei said Washington accepted some of Iran's seven conditions but left others unresolved; no talks until they are met. US blockade of Iranian ports continues. Dims last week's de-escalation hopes.

news.headline: Brent rises to $105.48 on weekend tanker attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi airports
news.summary: Drone strike near Sohar (Oman) and a projectile near Hormuz hit tankers; Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport killed 13 on 10-Oct. Goldman raised its Dec Brent forecast to $90. Safe-haven positive but feeds inflation and Fed-hike pricing.

news.headline: Gold posts weekly gain, spot $4,194; Dec futures settle $4,216.30
news.summary: Spot +1.5% Friday to a one-week high on bargain buying from the $4,066 two-month low; +1.3% on the week. StoneX sees a floor building near $4,000. FedWatch: 19% October hike, 84% by December.

news.headline: US September CPI due Wednesday: headline seen +0.6% m/m, 3.6% y/y; core +0.2%
news.summary: The week's key catalyst. A hot print would revive October/December hike bets and lift real yields; a soft core would support gold. PPI and retail sales follow Thursday.

news.headline: UMich sentiment drops to 46.3; 1-year inflation expectations jump to 4.7%

synthesis.overnight_summary: Gold ended last week up 1.3% at $4,194.6 and firmed to ~$4,208 in early Asia, testing Friday's high, after Iran called the US reply on reopening Hormuz 'insufficient' and weekend tanker and Houthi attacks pushed Brent to $105.5. The Fed backdrop is unchanged: October hike odds ~19%, December ~84%, real yields near 2.9%, with Wednesday's CPI (0.6% m/m expected) the week's big test. For MCX the bigger driver today is the rupee: RBI's weekend dollar curbs (oil-company dollar window from today, 20% reserve on hedges) lifted the rupee ~0.6% in thin NDF trade. The model gives +Rs 545 from COMEX and -882 from the rupee, a fair open near Rs 150,928 vs Friday's 1,51,265 (Rs 151,810 if the rupee opens flat). Expect a flat-to-lower MCX open despite firmer global gold; confirm against the 09:00 USD/INR open.
